security_audit.summary: Most backtick findings are false positives from Markdown text and code-fence parsing, not shell execution. The helper does read OpenAI-compatible credentials and can send supplied data context to an external LLM endpoint, while returning generated Python code that needs sandbox enforcement.

remediation.issue: OpenAI-compatible credentials are read from config, environment variables, and application settings.
remediation.suggestion: Document all credential access, avoid broad environment reads, and pass scoped credentials from a trusted host integration only.

remediation.issue: Data context and requirements are sent to an external LLM endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Add user-facing disclosure, redact sensitive fields before requests, and restrict base_url to approved endpoints when possible.

remediation.issue: Generated Python code is returned without validation in this helper.
remediation.suggestion: Add static checks for generated code and require execution inside a locked sandbox with no unapproved network or filesystem access.

content.value_statement: Data teams often need quick Python analysis code and consistent charts from changing requirements. This skill generates pandas-based scripts and reusable Matplotlib or Seaborn styling for sandboxed workflows.
actual_capabilities: Generates Python analysis scripts from a data context and requirement.
Prompts generated scripts to use pandas and save chart_output.png.
Provides a Matplotlib and Seaborn helper for professional chart styling.
Configures high-DPI figures with a fixed corporate color palette.
Extracts Python code blocks from model responses before returning code.
limitations: Requires OpenAI-compatible API configuration to generate analysis code.
Does not execute or validate generated Python code in this helper.
Depends on a sandbox with pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn installed.
May send data context and requirements to an external model endpoint.

use_cases.title: Create Exploratory Charts
use_cases.description: Generate a Python script that cleans a dataset summary and saves a first-pass visualization.

use_cases.title: Standardize Report Visuals
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent Seaborn and Matplotlib style across charts used in recurring reports.

use_cases.title: Prototype Analytics Workflows
use_cases.description: Turn a plain-language analysis requirement into a runnable script for review in a sandbox.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a CSV
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple dataset overview.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this data context to generate a pandas script that summarizes key columns and saves one clear bar chart.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Create analysis code that groups the data by segment, compares the main metric, and saves a labeled comparison chart.

prompt_templates.title: Find Trends and Outliers
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a script that parses date fields, plots the trend over time, and highlights likely outliers for review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Publication Chart
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a polished deliverable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce sandbox-ready Python code that cleans the data, creates a styled Seaborn visualization, and saves chart_output.png.

output_examples.input: A sales dataset summary with region, month, and revenue columns.
output_examples.output: The skill can return a pandas workflow that groups revenue by region and saves a styled bar chart for review.

output_examples.input: A customer activity table with signup date, plan, and monthly usage.
output_examples.output: The skill can produce an analysis plan that plots usage trends by plan and applies the shared visual theme.

output_examples.input: A quality metrics table with team, defect count, and reporting week.
output_examples.output: The skill can create a weekly trend chart and format it with readable labels, grid lines, and high-DPI output.

best_practices: Review generated code before execution, especially imports, file access, and network calls.
Run generated scripts only in a sandbox with approved data and scoped credentials.
Provide concise data summaries instead of raw sensitive records when requesting code.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated scripts directly on a production host.
Do not include secrets, customer identifiers, or regulated records in the data context.
Do not assume generated charts are accurate without checking the aggregation logic.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates Python analysis scripts and chart styling helpers for pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn workflows.

faq.question: Does it execute the generated code?
faq.answer: The included generator returns code as text. Execution must happen separately in a controlled sandbox.

faq.question: Which credentials can it use?
faq.answer: It can use an API key from role configuration, OPENAI_API_KEY, or application settings.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What chart libraries are supported?
faq.answer: The skill references pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn, with a helper for consistent plot styling.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a compact schema, sample rows, or aggregate context. Avoid secrets and sensitive personal data.
